title: Display switching/configuration OSD always appears on the top-left-most display
line: The Meta+P display switcher now opens on the primary (or built-in) screen instead of always on the top-left one.
explanation: The OSD service picks the right output (built-in, else primary) and calls QWindow::setScreen() on the selector. When Qt creates the window it re-derives the screen from the window geometry, which is still at (0,0), so the layer surface was requested on the output containing (0,0): the top-left one (WAYLAND_DEBUG showed get_layer_surface with the left output while the chosen QScreen was the right one). The fix also passes the screen to LayerShellQt::Window::setScreen(), which the layer surface uses directly.

commits.message:
osd: show the display switcher on the chosen screen

The selector was created as a layer surface on the window's screen,
which Qt reassigns from the window's default position at creation, so it
always opened on the top-left output. Pass the screen to layer-shell too.

BUG: 518584

patches.diff:
From e1e4a58abbf130176890aa82bb181eee91523450 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 05:48:57 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] osd: show the display switcher on the chosen screen

The selector was created as a layer surface on the window's screen,
which Qt reassigns from the window's default position at creation, so it
always opened on the top-left output. Pass the screen to layer-shell too.

BUG: 518584
---
 osd/osd.cpp | 1 +
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+)

diff --git a/osd/osd.cpp b/osd/osd.cpp
index 817da60f..61f08263 100644
--- a/osd/osd.cpp
+++ b/osd/osd.cpp
@@ -71,6 +71,7 @@ void Osd::showActionSelector()
     layerWindow->setLayer(LayerShellQt::Window::LayerOverlay);
     layerWindow->setAnchors({});
     layerWindow->setKeyboardInteractivity(LayerShellQt::Window::KeyboardInteractivityOnDemand);
+    layerWindow->setScreen(screen);
     m_osdActionSelector->setScreen(screen);
     m_osdActionSelector->setVisible(true);
 }
--

Same setup with the fix: the switcher opens on the primary right screen

review.text: Clean, exact one-line root-cause fix in kscreen's OSD: setting the chosen QScreen on LayerShellQt::Window prevents Qt's default (0,0) window geometry at creation from overriding the target wl_output to the top-left display. The WAYLAND_DEBUG trace, multi-monitor screenshots, and regression checks clearly prove the fix.

reviews.text: Clean, exact one-line root-cause fix in kscreen's OSD: setting the chosen QScreen on LayerShellQt::Window prevents Qt's default (0,0) window geometry at creation from overriding the target wl_output to the top-left display. The WAYLAND_DEBUG trace, multi-monitor screenshots, and regression checks clearly prove the fix.

OsdManager already picks the built-in output, else the primary one, which covers the reporter's laptop-plus-left-monitor setup. But the layer surface took its output from QWindow::screen(), which ended up on the output containing (0,0) when the window was created; the WAYLAND_DEBUG trace backs this up. Setting LayerShellQt::Window::setScreen(screen) is the dedicated layer-shell-qt API (non-deprecated since 6.6) for exactly this, so it is the right, minimal fix in the right repo. Before/after screenshots show the switcher moving from the left screen to the primary right one, with primary-swap and keyboard navigation checked. One-line diff, accurate message, BUG: 518584.
